key_insight: With a fixed measurement basis, gate-optimal repetition-code tomography needs only 0, 1 and 5 recovery gates for 3, 5 and 7 qubits, respectively, and correcting more sites is not always better.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing recovery can cut physical Pauli-gate overhead and improve precision, but poor conditioning—not gate count—limits scaling to larger codes.
method: Exhaustively enumerate recovery designs for 3-, 5- and 7-qubit repetition codes.
Determine rank using exact modular arithmetic at two primes.
Evaluate precision under a calibration-residual floor and estimate shot requirements.
evidence_signal: Across 40 sampled working points, a three-gate, three-qubit design was more precise than the standard six-gate decoder at every point, with a median improvement of 9.5×.
watch_item: The reported 10 mrad rms target requires 1.2×10^7 shots at a well-conditioned point; codes with 5 or more qubits remain impractical under the studied conditioning constraints.
paper_title: Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
